events.text:
This is game 35 in a series of 9×9 Go games. Each new game starts in a fresh session.

## Your goal

To become as strong at Go as you can: to keep improving, game after game, toward grandmaster-level play. The concrete target is to win consistently against the strongest opponent on the ladder, the 9d profile.

## What carries over

This session starts with no memory of the earlier ones: your conversation is not carried over. Your working directory does carry over: every file in it stays as you leave it. If CLAUDE.md exists there, it is loaded into your context at the start of every session; your other files are there to read with the file tools. What a later session knows of your earlier games is what you have left in these files.

Your working directory holds:
- CLAUDE.md (52,545 bytes)
- libs.py (1,378 bytes)

## This game

A new game. You play Black, so you move first.

Rules: Chinese area scoring, with 7 points of komi for White; a level score is a draw. Simple ko: an immediate recapture is refused, and the board marks the ko point when there is one. Suicide is not allowed. An invalid move is refused with the rule it broke, and the turn stays with you. The game ends after two passes in a row or a resignation; a game that reaches 243 moves is scored where it stands. After two passes the engine scores the position as it stands and decides itself which stones are dead.

## Opponents

Your opponent is KataGo playing in the style of a human of the rank you choose. The ladder, weakest to strongest: 20k, 18k, 16k, 14k, 12k, 10k, 8k, 6k, 4k, 2k, 1d, 3d, 5d, 7d, 9d. You choose the rank with `choose_opponent(rank)` before the first move; it holds for the whole game, and you choose again in the next game.

## Tools

- Go: `choose_opponent(rank)`, `board()`, `play(move)` with a point or `pass`, and `resign()`.
- Files: your Read, Write, Edit, Glob and Grep tools, for any file in your working directory.

You also have a shell, and you may write and run code in it; Python is available as `python3`. Use it only to inspect the current position and keep records — for example, to count stones or liberties, or check whether a move is legal. Do not build or use a Go engine, run Monte Carlo, search over sequences of future moves, or write a program that chooses, ranks or recommends moves.

## How this session ends

Play until the game is over. The final result comes back from your last Go call, followed by a closing note. Before you end the session after a game, write down in your working directory whatever will help the next session play better. The session ends when you end your turn.
I'm settling on black at 14k, using C3, G3, and E5 for the chord voicing.

Counting liberties here: my C6C7 group has two liberties at B6 and B7, while white's D6D7 group has liberties at D5 and D8. If I try playing D8 to reduce their liberties, that move only leaves my stone with one liberty at D9, which white can immediately capture by playing there -- so that doesn't work as a semeai tactic.

Trying D5 is pure suicide, and extending to B6 or B7 only gets me to three liberties, which still looks losing given I'm roughly 12 points behind overall. Looking at the white C8 stone's liberties, I consider B8 to pressure it, but white can respond with B6 to put my C6C7 group back in atari, forcing me to connect at B7.

Even after connecting, my group only reaches three liberties and white can simply defend C8 with C9 or D8. I'm starting to think sacrificing this invasion might be unavoidable, but losing by 12 means I need to keep fighting somehow — maybe there's eye space below toward B5/A5/B4, though that area is already contested by white's C4/C5 stones.

Maybe I should accept the C6/C7 loss as sacrifice stones, since white spends moves inside its own territory to capture them, leaving aji behind. I'm trying to recount the position more carefully by hand, tallying white's and black's stones to see where the territory actually sits.

Working through the count by region, I get roughly black 38 to white's larger total, putting me behind by around 12 points — I need a swing of six or more to catch up, which means I have to fight rather than settle. The D6D7 white group's connection points at D8 and D5 look like the weakness to target, since cutting there could split the position, though D8 remains white's key linking point even after pushing at F9.

Trying to work out a sequence capturing E2 for extra bottom territory and keeping C3 alive — but testing D2 as the key point leads to messy exchanges where white's C2 response creates complications and I end up losing a stone either way, so that line doesn't quite work cleanly. events.text: Checking line 491 against the Lessons entry confirms it matches up fine.

I lost game 35 (Black against the 14k opponent) by 2 points. Both of us passed at move 51, and the final area count was 43 for me against 38 + 7 komi for White.

- **Opening:** White took the left side with D4 and D7, and I took the right with G7, G3, E3 and F4. When I counted at move 22, I was behind by about 12.
- **Recovery:** At the bottom I strengthened my C3 stone with C2, then played D2 to cut White's E2 stone off from its support. That led to G2, an atari at E1, and F1 capturing 2 stones, which gave me the whole bottom edge and about 10 points.
- **Failed invasion:** My C7/C6 invasion of the top-left only ever had 2 liberties and died. Under area scoring it cost me nothing, but it gained nothing either. A couple of late tries there (C9, B6, A4, B8) didn't work, since White had an easy answer each time.
- **Where the last 2 points went:** White got the top edge (E8, E9, F9) after my E6/E7 moves. White's D3 also took away the base of my C3 corner stone early on.

I added the game record and these lessons to `CLAUDE.md`, including a plan for the next game: 14k again if I'm Black, 12k if I'm White. I also saved a new inspection-only script, `count.py`, which counts the area score once you tell it which stones are dead.
